newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast privatisation revenues around $180 mln.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast privatisation revenues around $180 mln.

text.p: Ivory Coast has earned about 100 billion CFA francs ($181.8 million) from the sale of state enterprises up to the end of last December, Prime Minister Daniel Kablan Duncan said on Wednesday.
The figure does not include about $190 million the state will receive from its ceding last week of a 51 percent stake in telephone company Ci-Telcom to France Telecom.
A total of 37 state firms have been sold off since 1994 from about 60 scheduled for privatisation, Duncan said in a speech flagging off Privatisation Open Days in Abidjan.
Ivory Coast has been praised by World Bank officials for the execution of its privatisation programme whose objective is to draw in foreign capital and expertise to spur economic growth.
Government critics have denounced what they term a cheap sell-off of the state's patrimony but the main opposition parties are not against the principle of privatisation.
The government has conducted an advertising blitz to encourage Ivorians to become share owners, but only a small fraction of state assets have so far been offered on the Abidjan Stock Exchange.

In the case of Ci-Telcom, the largest item on the programme, only 10 to 15 percent of the capital will be sold on the bourse, but the state could offload some of its remaining 35 percent holding later.
Other important enterprises already sold include water and electricity monopolies, banks and agri-industrial holdings.
Important companies still on the list include national carrier Air Ivoire, the Hotel Ivoire in Abidjan and the President in the political capital Yamoussoukro and a refinery in Abidjan.
